earlier_scan.source_named: Only survey/wordlist materials exist (Potter & Kassell 2004 SIL survey report; Ross 1988 comparative); no grammar or phonology of Toura (PNG) found.

sources.citation: SIL PNG 'Language Resources: Toura' page and SIL Language & Culture Archives search for [don] (Wayback snapshots 2015); Glottolog 5.3 languoid tour1243; Wikipedia 'Toura language (Papua New Guinea)'
sources.note: Catalogue pages: SIL lists exactly one item for Toura (Kassell & Potter 2011); Glottolog med = wordlist_or_less, 0 descriptive refs; Wikipedia stub notes PARADISEC audio collections only.

sources.citation: Kassell, Alison and Margaret Potter. 2011. A sociolinguistic profile of the Abadi language group. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2011-030. Dallas: SIL International. 59 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Survey of Lala, Abadi and Toura (June-July 2003). Sec. 8.1 'Characteristics of the language' lists phones of Abadi only. Appendix A.4 (pp. 53-58) gives two Toura wordlists (Akuku, Toromoku villages) in phonetic transcription with no stress marks (0 occurrences of the IPA stress mark in the text layer). Only Toura item listed by SIL PNG and the SIL archive for [don].

sources.citation: Lynch, John, Malcolm Ross and Terry Crowley. 2002. The Oceanic languages. Richmond: Curzon. (pp. 54-55)
sources.note: Nothing. Doura mentioned only as a member of the 'Proto B' Central Papuan subgroup (t > k innovation) in the comparative-method illustration; no sketch of Doura.

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm. 1988. Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian languages of western Melanesia (Pacific Linguistics C-98). Canberra: ANU. (Central Papuan section pp. 190-212)
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online: WID Offsite Storage PL6201.R67 1988 (also: archive.org controlled lending)
sources.note: Nothing on Doura stress. Doura appears in the Central Papuan consonant-correspondence tables (pp. 192, 205) and cognate sets; data source given as 'Dutton n.d.' (Appendix B). Stress mentions in the book concern other languages (Ali, Yabem area).

sources.citation: Pawley, Andrew. 1976. Austronesian languages: western part of south-eastern mainland Papua. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 2 (Pacific Linguistics C-39), 301-319. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. p. 301, source list: "DOURA. Spoken by several hundred in three to six villages around the eastern side of Galley Reach. No published grammar or dictionary."

sources.citation: Pawley, Andrew. 1975. The relationship of the Austronesian languages of Central Papua: a preliminary study. In T. E. Dutton (ed.), Studies in languages of central and south-east Papua (Pacific Linguistics C-29), 3-106. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing on Doura stress. Sec. 3.6 Doura (pp. 13-14): 3-6 villages east of Galley Reach; data from Mr Kere Moi (UPNG student, 1969). Rest is comparative sound correspondences and lexicostatistics. The one stress rule in the volume (p. 109, 'Stress is unmarked but always occurs on the first syllable of bisyllabic words and on the second last syllable of words of more than two syllables') belongs to Kolia's Balawaia (Sinaugoro) sketch, not Doura.

sources.citation: Ray, Sidney H. 1907. The Melanesian languages of British New Guinea. In Reports of the Cambridge Anthropological Expedition to Torres Straits, vol. III: Linguistics, 413-503. Cambridge: CUP.
sources.note: Nothing. Doura occurs only in the language/locality list, the numeral table (p. 470) and the comparative vocabulary; Ray's Doura data are 'MS., Rev. J. Chalmers. Printed in British New Guinea Vocabularies, 1889'. No grammatical or phonological notes for Doura; no 'accent'/'stress' lines anywhere in the British New Guinea section.

sources.citation: Potter, Margaret and Alison Kassell. 2004. Toura language survey report. SIL-PNG unpublished manuscript, 49 pp. (Glottolog 106462)
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The only Toura-specific document known; by analogy with the same authors' 2011 Abadi report it probably contains a 'characteristics of the language' section (phones, word order) and Toura wordlists; a stress remark is possible but not likely.

sources.citation: Ray, Sidney H. 1929. The languages of the Central Division of Papua. Journal of the Royal Anthropological Institute 59: 65-96.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held

sources.note: Ray's grammatical notes on Central Division languages sometimes include a line on accent; Doura is among the languages covered (Glottolog: wordlist-level). Now US public domain; HathiTrust full view exists but blocked bot access.

sources.citation: Chalmers, James (MS). Doura vocabulary, printed in British New Guinea Vocabularies (London: SPCK, 1889); reused by Ray 1907.

sources.note: Earliest Doura data; missionary vocabularies occasionally mark accent. Not found on archive.org by title search.
